standard_prerequisites.name: Finite central skew field extensions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the description of the Brauer group as consisting of classes of finite central skew field extensions of the ground field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that it suffices to show that a finite central skew field extension of an algebraically closed field is the field itself.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite integral subalgebras of a field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the subalgebra generated by one element of a skew field is a commutative finite integral algebra over the field and hence a field.

core_obligations: The elementwise argument (proof lines 671-676): for a finite central skew field extension and an element of it, the subalgebra generated by that element over the ground field is a commutative finite integral algebra, hence a field by the cited lemma, and since the ground field is algebraically closed that field is the ground field itself.
Conclusion (proof lines 676-677): since the element was arbitrary, the skew field equals the ground field, so no nontrivial class remains and the Brauer group is zero.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to showing that a finite central skew field extension is the ground field.
Show that each element generates a finite integral subalgebra, which is a field.
Use algebraic closedness to conclude that the element lies in the ground field.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the Brauer group of an algebraically closed field is zero (statement lines 666-669). The proof is a complete argument: for a finite central skew field extension and an arbitrary element, the subalgebra generated by the element is a commutative finite integral algebra over the ground field and hence a field by a named result of the Algebra chapter; algebraic closedness forces that field to be the ground field, and since the element was arbitrary the extension is trivial (proof lines 671-677). The non-formal content is the elementwise reduction. The claim is H2.
